location_note: 'Exhibition Tunnel' excavation on the summit of the City of David, next to the Giv'ati Parking Lot; no map reference. Placed by the title name Jerusalem (Z4).
notes: First detailed record of a cistern (hewn shaft L173, tunnel L247; Stratum VI, Early Roman) into which a 1st-c. CE assemblage of 4,887 sherds and vessels (49.5% cooking vessels) was dumped, putting it out of use. The dumped assemblage is not coded as hoard_cache: the report calls it dumped/deposited refuse, not concealed (choice C8). Other cooking-pot contexts (Jewish Quarter cisterns and miqveh, Area J, etc.) are cited from earlier work; not coded.

features.subtype: rock-hewn cistern with shaft L173 and tunnel L247, filled with a 1st-c. CE pottery dump
features.period: Early Roman (Stratum VI); filled in the 1st c. CE
features.quote: a cistern was found, consisting of a hewn shaft (L173) and tunnel
